messages:
maria: heads up — during the dedicated canary deploy just now we saw a short burst of 503s from the frontends that correlate with concurrent prefix demote + eviction activity. filing here before i forget. :eyes:
ajay: can you paste the logs? was it demote path (graceful demote) or a hard eviction?
maria: small snippet from router logs we captured:
```
2026-03-21T14:02:12Z router: req id=aa12 path=/predict tenant=acme status=503 backend_err=cache_miss_and_evict
2026-03-21T14:02:12Z runtime: demote ack prefix=acct:123 gen=42 -> demoted
2026-03-21T14:02:12Z eviction: scanner removed prefix=acct:123 slab=4 reason=aging
```
maria: looks like demote ack and eviction scan ran effectively concurrently; client requests hit between demote and the slab residency change. i think we returned 503 instead of reading-through or falling back. :thinking:
kelsey: ugh. i've seen this pattern in prod once when the demote path doesn't publish a transient "in-flight" state to the router. router assumes eviction means not-resident and 503s instead of routing to fallback.
oliver: do we have a contract that demote must be visible to routing before eviction-complete? currently the runtime emits demote->ack immediately and then background compaction/evict removes slab entries. there isn't a strict ordering guarantee other than eventual consistency.
ajay: that contract gap is the problem. two options i see: 1) make demote synchronous w.r.t router visibility (block until a soft-residency marker propogates) or 2) add a short "post-demote grace window" during which router will try fallback reads instead of 503.
tom: option 1 increases latency on demote calls and could block hotkey handoffs. option 2 is faster but risks more wasted work if eviction actually completes quickly. both are doable.
infra-bot: smoke test finished on canary (deploy-2026-03-21-14:00): 10k requests/sec for 2m, observed 0.12% 503s during one burst.
maria: my vote is option 2 as a short-term mitigation: add a configurable 50-200ms post-demote grace where router treats demoted prefixes as "read-through allowed" and routes to fallback model variant instead of returning 503. low ops blast radius and quick rollback.
kelsey: agreed for quick mitigation. longer-term we should define a clear runtime->router contract: demote has states [inflight, demoted-visible, evicted] with generation tags and idempotent transitions. that lets us reason about reads during transitions without heuristics.
ajay: +1. i'll sketch a tiny RFC: propose generation-tagged demote ack that includes expected eviction ETA (best-effort) and a boolean 'allow-readthrough' hint. router uses that to decide fallback attempts. if ETA expired, router treats as evicted.
oliver: also add telemetry: counters for requests observed while prefix in demoted-visible state, and per-prefix last-demote-gen. that will let us tune grace window.
tom: short-term tasks: (1) runtime: emit demote hint + gen (2) router: honor hint for N ms default 100ms (config), fall back to existing behavior if hint missing (3) ops: enable canary with 100ms grace and monitor.
maria: OK i'll open the RFC + a small patch with the runtime hint tonight. ajay can you take the router side PR tomorrow morning? i'll own telem + canary coord.
ajay: yep will do.
kelsey: let's also add an integration test that simulates demote+evict interleaving so we don't regress.
mar ia: (typo) maria: good call. will add test matrix. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: created ticket INF-4281 "demote->evict visibility contract + router grace" and linked canary job.
maria: thanks. once RFC is up i'll @everyone for review. keeping this thread for quick updates.
